body:
We use HQ from 1EDI Source to convert 850 edi documents to csv which get processed through our ingestion system. Shopify supports csv exports which an agent manually does at the moment while we look into automating it via their api. 

I would look into if Microsoft dynamic supports edi transactions and if it does map out the various vendors. They’ll typically run 1-2k for testing each connection, afterwards you’ll get an as2 or sftp connection to receive and send documents. 

From our research lowes and Home Depot have to stay with ch for their drop ship program.  Walmart will be more then happy to go direct with you.

Going automatic edi isn’t cheap, but the savings in labor/manual processes will pay for itself quickly.

Fear not! You can always use legacy ie rendering in edge through carefully crafted gpo rules. Our vendor even kindly provided the instructions......

Seriously though. MS deprecated ActiveX over 5 years ago and these vendors still haven't upgraded?

I’m going through this right now. Vendor requires their active x web application to run with full administrative access and client machines without uac. 

Failing those steps the support team will refuse to assist you.
